Overview

Embark on an extraordinary 14-day journey through Skardu and Hunza Valley, where winter and spring bring breathtaking landscapes, frozen lakes, snow-covered mountains, and vibrant cultural encounters. This trip is perfect for adventure seekers, photographers, and nature lovers, offering an immersive experience in the heart of the Karakoram region.

Why This Tour?

  • Stunning Winter & Spring Landscapes – Witness frozen lakes, snow-draped valleys, and blooming orchards as the seasons transition.
  • Cultural Immersion – Explore ancient forts, interact with local communities, and experience authentic Balti and Hunza traditions.
  • Breathtaking Scenic Routes – Travel along the Karakoram Highway, visit Khaplu, Shigar, and Naltar Valley, and explore some of the highest plateaus in the world.
  • Luxury & Comfort – Enjoy hand-picked accommodations, expert-guided experiences, and seamless transportation throughout the journey.

Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad – Welcome to Pakistan

Upon arrival at Islamabad International Airport, you will be greeted by our team and transferred to your hotel. After check-in, take some time to unwind before meeting your fellow travelers at a welcome dinner. If time permits, explore the bustling capital and experience its unique blend of modernity and tradition.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 2: Journey to Chilas – Scenic Drive Through Hazara & Kohistan

Begin your road adventure towards Chilas, passing through the picturesque Hazara Motorway and Karakoram Highway. Enjoy a scenic drive through lush valleys, making stops at Besham, Kohistan, and Dasu. Upon arrival in Chilas, check into your hotel and enjoy a relaxing evening in the peaceful town.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Shangrila Hotel Chilas
  • Luxury: Shangrila Hotel Chilas
  • Standard: Indus Lodges Chilas

Day 3: Entering Skardu Valley – Land of the Giants

Today, embark on a stunning drive along the Indus River as you make your way to Skardu Valley. Stop at Junction Point, where the Himalayas, Karakoram, and Hindu Kush ranges meet, creating a spectacular landscape. Pass through Astak Nala and Alam Bridge, finally reaching Skardu, where you’ll check in and enjoy a relaxed evening.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Byarsa Hotel
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 4: Exploring Skardu & Shigar – The Heart of Baltistan

After breakfast, visit Lower and Upper Kachura Lakes, where the stunning reflections of the mountains on the water create a mesmerizing sight. Continue towards Shigar Valley, passing through the Cold Desert and Blind Lake, before arriving at the magnificent Shigar Fort, a 17th-century heritage site. Take in the serene atmosphere of Shigar village before returning to your hotel.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Shigar Fort
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 5: Journey to Khaplu – The Valley of Kings

Head towards the beautiful Khaplu Valley, making stops at scenic viewpoints along the way. Visit Sailing Village, Khaplu Palace, and nearby ancient mosques, all offering insights into Baltistan’s royal history. Enjoy free time to wander through traditional Balti settlements before settling in for the night.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Khaplu Palace
  • Luxury: Destination Hotel
  • Standard: North Homes

Day 6: Discovering Manthoka Waterfall & Sadpara Lake

Begin your day with a visit to Manthoka Waterfall, a spectacular natural wonder surrounded by rugged cliffs. Afterward, drive towards Sadpara Lake, a pristine alpine reservoir that supplies water to Skardu. Take in the tranquil scenery before heading back to your hotel for the night.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Byarsa Hotel
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 7: Heritage Tour in Hunza Valley

Depart early for Hunza Valley, stopping at Astak Nala and Alam Bridge along the way. Take in the panoramic views at Rakaposhi View Point before reaching Karimabad, the heart of Hunza. Explore Baltit Fort, Altit Fort, and the lively Karimabad Bazaar before heading up to Duikar Viewpoint for a spectacular sunset.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hunza Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Eagles Nest Hotel
  • Standard: Ayash Resort

Day 8: Attabad Lake & Gojal Valley Adventures

Begin the day with a drive through the Attabad Tunnels before arriving at Attabad Lake, known for its surreal blue waters and scenic beauty. Continue to Gulmit Village, where you can hike up to Ondra Poyga Viewpoint for breathtaking panoramic landscapes. Return for a relaxing evening by the lake.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Luxus Resort Hunza
  • Luxury: Famree Resort

Standard: Silk Route Lodge

Day 9: Journey to Khunjerab Pass – The Pak-China Border

Drive through Hussaini Suspension Bridge and Passu Village, stopping to admire the imposing Passu Cones (Cathedral Peaks). Continue towards Khunjerab National Park, home to rare wildlife, before reaching Khunjerab Pass, the highest international border in the world.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Luxus Resort Hunza
  • Luxury: Famree Resort
  • Standard: Silk Route Lodge

Day 10: Explore Nagar Valley & Hoper Glacier

A visit to Nagar Valley offers spectacular views of lush meadows and Hoper Glacier, a remarkable site where the ice meets the mountains. Enjoy a short hike before returning to Hunza for a relaxing evening.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hunza Serena Inn
  • Luxury: Eagles Nest Hotel
  • Standard: Ayash Resort

Day 11: Naltar Valley – A Hidden Alpine Gem

Depart for Naltar Valley, passing through Nomal Village before arriving at the Naltar Wildlife Sanctuary. Visit Satrangi Lake, known for its vibrant, multicolored reflections. Later, continue towards Gilgit for the night.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Gilgit Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Riverdale Hotel
  • Standard: Mandarin Inn

Day 12: Return Journey to Besham

Begin the return trip with a drive towards Besham, stopping at various viewpoints and local markets along the way. Enjoy an overnight stay in this peaceful town before the final leg of the journey.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hilton Hotel Besham
  • Luxury: Hilton Hotel Besham
  • Standard: Besham Inn

Day 13: Islamabad City Tour – Exploring the Capital

Back in Islamabad, explore Faisal Mosque, Pakistan Monument, and Daman-e-Koh, followed by free time for shopping or dining in the city. Enjoy a final dinner before heading back to the hotel.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 14: Departure – Farewell Pakistan

Conclude your journey with a transfer to the airport for your flight home, taking with you unforgettable memories of Skardu and Hunza’s breathtaking landscapes and warm hospitality.

Packing List

Spring Packing Checklist for Northern Pakistan - Summit Experts

Spring (late-March to May) is one of the best seasons to explore Northern Pakistan, with mild weather, blooming flowers, and lush green landscapes. To make sure you have a comfortable and enjoyable journey, we’ve prepared a comprehensive packing list for your adventure.

Essential Packing Categories:

  1. Luggage & Bags
    • Main Luggage (70-80L): A sturdy, spacious bag for all your essentials. Ensure it has waterproof covers for unexpected weather.
    • Daypack (30-40L): Ideal for carrying daily items like snacks, water, and your camera during excursions.
    • Padlocks: Secure your belongings during travel.
  2. Clothing
    • Upper Body:
      • Lightweight Jacket: Perfect for chilly mornings and evenings. Consider a windbreaker or fleece.
      • Long-Sleeve Shirts & T-Shirts: Comfortable, breathable fabrics are ideal for layering.
      • Rain Jacket: Waterproof and wind-resistant for unexpected spring showers.
    • Lower Body:
      • Trekking Trousers: Lightweight and quick-drying trousers for hikes and outdoor activities.
      • Comfortable Pants/Jeans: Suitable for both city tours and countryside visits.
    • General Tips:
      • Layer Up: The weather can vary, so layers will help you adjust to temperature changes.
      • Respect Local Culture: Modest clothing is recommended, especially in towns and cultural sites.
  3. Footwear
    • Hiking Boots: Well-worn, waterproof boots with good ankle support for trekking.
    • Comfortable Walking Shoes: For city exploration and casual outings.
    • Warm Socks: Preferably made of moisture-wicking material.
  4. Accessories
    • Sunblock (SPF 50+): Protects against strong UV rays.
    • Hat/Cap: For sun protection during hikes and outdoor tours.
    • Sunglasses: Good UV protection for your eyes.
    • Light Scarf/Bandana: Useful for dust protection and sun cover.
  5. Toiletries & Personal Care
    • Compact Toiletry Kit: Include essentials like toothpaste, deodorant, and moisturizer.
    • Travel Towel: Quick-drying and lightweight.
    • Wet Wipes & Hand Sanitizer: For maintaining hygiene during day trips.
  6. Hydration & Snacks
    • Reusable Water Bottle (Insulated Preferred): Stay hydrated, especially during hikes.
    • Energy Bars & Snacks: Lightweight snacks for quick energy boosts.
  7. Tech & Gadgets
    • Camera & Accessories: Capture stunning landscapes and cultural moments. Bring extra memory cards.
    • Power Bank: Essential for keeping devices charged on the go.
    • Travel Adapter: Ensure compatibility with local sockets.
  8. Important Documents
    • Passport: Must have at least six months of validity remaining.
    • Visa & Travel Insurance: Check visa requirements and carry printouts of your insurance details.
    • Emergency Contact Information: A printed list of important contacts.

Tips for Spring Travel

  • Prepare for Variable Weather: Spring can bring unexpected showers, so a waterproof jacket and protective covers for your belongings are recommended.
  • Comfortable Layers: Temperatures fluctuate, so plan for both warm afternoons and cool evenings.
  • Be Ready for Long Walks: Comfortable shoes and a light backpack will make your excursions more enjoyable.

Why Travel with Summit Experts?

Our experienced team ensures that your journey is not just comfortable, but also safe and unforgettable. We provide personalized packing recommendations based on your specific tour itinerary, and our guides are always ready to help you with any last-minute needs.

Overview

Experience the splendor of Gilgit-Baltistan on this spectacular 12-day aerial adventure covering Skardu and Hunza Valley during summer and autumn. This journey combines striking landscapes, rich cultural heritage, and unique adventures, offering travelers a captivating blend of beauty, history, and comfort.

Why This Tour?

  • Majestic Landscapes – Explore Deosai National Park, Khunjerab National Park, Attabad Lake, and more.
  • Cultural Insight – Visit historic sites like Shigar Fort, Baltit Fort, and Khaplu Palace.
  • Comfortable Travel – Enjoy air travel convenience, premium accommodations, and professional guidance.
  • Adventure & Leisure – Perfect balance of exciting adventures and relaxing explorations.

Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad

Arrive at Islamabad International Airport, where our team will warmly greet you and escort you to your hotel. After settling in, join the group for dinner and explore Islamabad at your leisure.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 2: Skardu & Shigar Valley

Fly to Skardu, exploring its scenic beauty upon arrival. Visit the serene Lower and Upper Kachura Lakes, then depart for Shigar Valley, stopping at the Cold Desert and Blind Lake. Discover the historic Shigar Fort.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Shigar Fort
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 3: Deosai National Park

Journey to Deosai National Park, stopping at Manthal Buddha and Sadpara Lake. Enjoy breathtaking views at Bara Pani and Kala Pani, visit Sheosar Lake, and immerse yourself in Deosai’s untouched beauty.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Shigar Fort
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana or Qayyam Hotel
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 4: Bashu Valley

Experience an adventurous off-road drive to the picturesque Bashu Valley. Explore its natural beauty, relax, and take in the stunning surroundings before returning to Skardu.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Byarsa Hotel
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 5: Hunza Valley – Heritage Tour

Depart early for Hunza Valley, enjoying scenic stops including Rakaposhi View Point and the Junction Point of three mountain ranges. Visit historic Baltit Fort, Karimabad Bazaar, Altit Fort, and the stunning viewpoint at Duikar.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hunza Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Eagles Nest Hotel
  • Standard: Ayash Resort

Day 6: Gojal Valley – Attabad and Gulmit Village

Travel through the scenic Attabad Tunnels to Gojal Valley, visiting Attabad Lake. Explore Gulmit Village, hike the Ondra Poyga trail, and relax amid Gojal’s beauty.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Luxus Resort Hunza
  • Luxury: Famree Resort
  • Standard: Silk Route Lodge

Day 7: Khunjerab National Park

Explore Khunjerab National Park, visiting iconic sites like Hussaini Suspension Bridge and the picturesque Passu Village. Enjoy wildlife spotting on your way to the Pak-China border.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Luxus Resort Hunza
  • Luxury: Famree Resort
  • Standard: Silk Route Lodge

Day 8: Nagar Valley – Hoper Glacier View Point

Visit Nagar Valley, stopping at Hoper Glacier viewpoint. Take a short hike for closer glacier views, and enjoy leisure time before returning to Hunza.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hunza Serena Inn
  • Luxury: Eagles Nest Hotel
  • Standard: Ayash Resort

Day 9: Naltar Valley – Satrangi Lake

Head to Naltar Valley, visiting the Wildlife Sanctuary and the stunning Satrangi Lake. Later, explore Gilgit city, visiting Kargah Buddha and NLI Market.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Gilgit Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Riverdale Hotel
  • Standard: Mandarian Inn

Day 10: Islamabad – Leisure Day

Fly back to Islamabad, check into your hotel, and relax. Join the team for dinner and enjoy free time exploring the city.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 11: Islamabad City Tour

Visit Islamabad’s iconic landmarks, including Faisal Mosque, Pakistan Monument, and the scenic Daman-e-Koh viewpoint. Spend the day exploring the vibrant capital.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 12: Departure

Transfer to Islamabad International Airport for your return flight home, cherishing unforgettable memories of Gilgit-Baltistan.

  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 4: Bashu Valley

Experience an adventurous off-road drive to the picturesque Bashu Valley. Explore its natural beauty, relax, and take in the stunning surroundings before returning to Skardu.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Byarsa Hotel
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 5: Hunza Valley – Heritage Tour

Depart early for Hunza Valley, enjoying scenic stops including Rakaposhi View Point and the Junction Point of three mountain ranges. Visit historic Baltit Fort, Karimabad Bazaar, Altit Fort, and the stunning viewpoint at Duikar.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hunza Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Eagles Nest Hotel
  • Standard: Ayash Resort

Day 6: Gojal Valley – Attabad and Gulmit Village

Travel through the scenic Attabad Tunnels to Gojal Valley, visiting Attabad Lake. Explore Gulmit Village, hike the Ondra Poyga trail, and relax amid Gojal’s beauty.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Luxus Resort Hunza
  • Luxury: Famree Resort
  • Standard: Silk Route Lodge

Day 7: Khunjerab National Park

Explore Khunjerab National Park, visiting iconic sites like Hussaini Suspension Bridge and the picturesque Passu Village. Enjoy wildlife spotting on your way to the Pak-China border.

Stay Options:

  • Luxury: Famree Resort
  • Standard: Silk Route Lodge

Day 8: Nagar Valley – Hoper Glacier View Point

Visit Nagar Valley, stopping at Hoper Glacier viewpoint. Take a short hike for closer glacier views, and enjoy leisure time before returning to Hunza.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hunza Serena Inn
  • Luxury: Eagles Nest Hotel
  • Standard: Ayash Resort

Day 9: Naltar Valley – Satrangi Lake

Head to Naltar Valley, visiting the Wildlife Sanctuary and the stunning Satrangi Lake. Later, explore Gilgit city, visiting Kargah Buddha and NLI Market.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Gilgit Serena Hotel

  • Standard: Mandarian Inn

Day 10: Islamabad – Leisure Day

Fly back to Islamabad, check into your hotel, and relax. Join the team for dinner and enjoy free time exploring the city.

Stay Options:

  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel

Visit Islamabad’s iconic landmarks, including Faisal Mosque, Pakistan Monument, and the scenic Daman-e-Koh viewpoint. Spend the day exploring the vibrant capital.

Packing List

Packing Checklist for Northern Pakistan - Summit Experts

Traveling to the scenic mountains of Northern Pakistan during summer and autumn (June to mid-November) requires smart packing. The weather is cool and crisp, and the landscapes are stunning, making it an ideal time for a memorable journey. To ensure you have everything you need, here’s our recommended packing list.

Essential Packing Categories:

  1. Luggage & Bags
    • Main Bag (70-80L): A sturdy, spacious bag for all your essentials. Consider a duffel or rucksack with waterproof covers.
    • Carry-On/Daypack (30-40L): Ideal for carrying daily items and essentials during flights and local travel.
    • Padlocks: For added security during travel.
  2. Clothing
    • Upper Body:
      • Insulated Jacket: Lightweight but warm, perfect for layering.
      • Fleece or Soft Shell Jacket: To keep warm without feeling too bulky.
      • Long-Sleeve Shirts & T-Shirts: Preferably quick-drying fabrics.
    • Lower Body:
      • Trekking Trousers: Comfortable, quick-drying trousers suitable for hikes.
      • Thermal Underwear: For colder days and nights.
    • General Tips:
      • Layers are Key: Autumn weather can be unpredictable; layering helps you adjust to changes in temperature.
      • Modest Clothing: Covering shoulders and knees is recommended in urban areas and when visiting cultural sites.
  3. Footwear
    • Hiking Boots: Well-worn, waterproof boots with good ankle support.
    • Warm Socks: Opt for wool or moisture-wicking material.
    • Extra Laces: Just in case.
  4. Accessories
    • Sunglasses & Sunblock (SPF 50+): The sun can be strong, even in cooler weather.
    • Hat/Cap: For sun protection.
    • Warm Beanie: Essential for cooler mornings and evenings.
  5. Toiletries & Personal Care
    • Travel Towel & Wet Wipes: Compact and quick-drying options.
    • Basic Hygiene Kit: Include toothpaste, deodorant, lip balm, and moisturizers.
    • Hand Sanitizer & Masks: Always useful.
  6. Hydration & Snacks
    • Water Bottle (Insulated Recommended): Carry at least a 1L bottle for day trips.
    • Energy Snacks: Granola bars, dried fruits, and nuts for quick energy during hikes.
  7. Tech & Gadgets
    • Camera & Spare Batteries: Capture the beauty of autumn landscapes. Bring extra memory cards.
    • Power Bank: To keep devices charged during long excursions.
  8. Important Documents
    • Passport: With at least six months of validity and two blank pages.
    • Visa & Travel Insurance: Check requirements and ensure you have printouts of all travel documents.
    • Emergency Contacts: Keep a printed list of important contact numbers.

Tips for Autumn and Summer Packing

  • Plan for Cool Nights: While days can be mild, temperatures drop quickly in the evenings. A warm jacket and thermal wear will be your best friends.
  • Pack Light but Smart: Choose versatile clothing that can be mixed and matched.
  • Respect Local Culture: While locals are friendly, it’s respectful to dress modestly, especially in towns and when visiting religious sites.

Why Travel with Summit Experts?

Our tours are designed with your comfort and safety in mind. We make sure you’re prepared for every aspect of your trip so that you can focus on enjoying the beauty of Northern Pakistan.

Overview

Embark on a breathtaking 14-day road adventure through the awe-inspiring landscapes of Skardu and Hunza Valley during summer and autumn. This tour offers an immersive experience of Pakistan’s northern areas, combining scenic beauty, historical landmarks, and cultural insights with comfortable travel and accommodations.

Why This Tour?

    • Scenic Routes – Travel via iconic roads such as the Karakoram Highway, exploring valleys, glaciers, and mountains.
    • Cultural Heritage – Visit renowned forts and palaces including Baltit Fort, Shigar Fort, and Khaplu Palace.
    • Diverse Landscapes – From lush valleys and turquoise lakes to rugged mountain passes and vast glaciers.
    • Adventure & Comfort – Perfect blend of exciting explorations and leisure time in premium hotels.

  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Adventure off-road to Bashu Valley. Explore this beautiful valley and relax before returning to Skardu.

Early departure for Hunza Valley. Visit the Junction Point, Rakaposhi View Point, Baltit Fort, Karimabad Bazaar, Altit Fort, and Duikar viewpoint.

Visit Gojal Valley, passing Attabad Tunnels and Lake. Explore Gulmit Village and hike Ondra Poyga trail.

  • Premium: Luxus Resort Hunza

Drive to Khunjerab National Park, stopping at Hussaini Suspension Bridge, Passu Village, and Pak-China border. Spot wildlife en route.

Packing Checklist for Northern Pakistan - Summit Experts

Traveling to the scenic mountains of Northern Pakistan during summer and autumn (June to mid-November) requires smart packing. The weather is cool and crisp, and the landscapes are stunning, making it an ideal time for a memorable journey. To ensure you have everything you need, here’s our recommended packing list.

Essential Packing Categories:

  1. Luggage & Bags
    • Main Bag (70-80L): A sturdy, spacious bag for all your essentials. Consider a duffel or rucksack with waterproof covers.
    • Carry-On/Daypack (30-40L): Ideal for carrying daily items and essentials during flights and local travel.
    • Padlocks: For added security during travel.
  2. Clothing
    • Upper Body:
      • Insulated Jacket: Lightweight but warm, perfect for layering.
      • Fleece or Soft Shell Jacket: To keep warm without feeling too bulky.
      • Long-Sleeve Shirts & T-Shirts: Preferably quick-drying fabrics.
    • Lower Body:
      • Trekking Trousers: Comfortable, quick-drying trousers suitable for hikes.
      • Thermal Underwear: For colder days and nights.
    • General Tips:
      • Layers are Key: Autumn weather can be unpredictable; layering helps you adjust to changes in temperature.
      • Modest Clothing: Covering shoulders and knees is recommended in urban areas and when visiting cultural sites.
  3. Footwear
    • Hiking Boots: Well-worn, waterproof boots with good ankle support.
    • Warm Socks: Opt for wool or moisture-wicking material.
    • Extra Laces: Just in case.
  4. Accessories
    • Sunglasses & Sunblock (SPF 50+): The sun can be strong, even in cooler weather.
    • Hat/Cap: For sun protection.
    • Warm Beanie: Essential for cooler mornings and evenings.
  5. Toiletries & Personal Care
    • Travel Towel & Wet Wipes: Compact and quick-drying options.
    • Basic Hygiene Kit: Include toothpaste, deodorant, lip balm, and moisturizers.
    • Hand Sanitizer & Masks: Always useful.
  6. Hydration & Snacks
    • Water Bottle (Insulated Recommended): Carry at least a 1L bottle for day trips.
    • Energy Snacks: Granola bars, dried fruits, and nuts for quick energy during hikes.
  7. Tech & Gadgets
    • Camera & Spare Batteries: Capture the beauty of autumn landscapes. Bring extra memory cards.
    • Power Bank: To keep devices charged during long excursions.
  8. Important Documents
    • Passport: With at least six months of validity and two blank pages.
    • Visa & Travel Insurance: Check requirements and ensure you have printouts of all travel documents.
    • Emergency Contacts: Keep a printed list of important contact numbers.

Tips for Autumn and Summer Packing

  • Plan for Cool Nights: While days can be mild, temperatures drop quickly in the evenings. A warm jacket and thermal wear will be your best friends.
  • Pack Light but Smart: Choose versatile clothing that can be mixed and matched.
  • Respect Local Culture: While locals are friendly, it’s respectful to dress modestly, especially in towns and when visiting religious sites.

Overview

Discover the enchanting Skardu Valley on this remarkable 9-day aerial adventure, perfect for experiencing the breathtaking beauty of Gilgit-Baltistan during the vibrant summer and autumn months. Explore picturesque landscapes, pristine lakes, majestic waterfalls, and rich cultural heritage with comfort and convenience. This itinerary offers unforgettable experiences, blending scenic beauty, cultural exploration, and thrilling adventure.

Why This Tour?

    • Spectacular Landscapes – Marvel at the striking beauty of Deosai National Park, Shigar, Khaplu, and Bashu Valleys.
    • Cultural Exploration – Visit historic forts like Shigar and Khaplu Palaces and experience local traditions.
    • Adventure and Relaxation – Perfect blend of outdoor adventure and leisurely exploration.
    • Comfortable Travel – Smooth air and road travel, luxurious accommodations, and professional guides.

Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad

Arrive at Islamabad International Airport, where our team will warmly welcome you and transfer you to your hotel. Rest, meet your fellow travelers over dinner, and enjoy free time exploring the vibrant capital city.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 2: Skardu & Shigar Valley

Fly to Skardu, exploring its stunning valley upon arrival. Visit Lower and Upper Kachura Lakes before heading to Shigar Valley, stopping at the mesmerizing Cold Desert and Blind Lake. Explore historic Shigar Fort and its charming surroundings.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Shigar Fort
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana or Qayyam Hotel
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 3: Deosai National Park

Depart for Deosai National Park, stopping at Manthal Buddha and Sadpara Lake. Journey through Bara Pani and Kala Pani to Sheosar Lake, savoring the incredible landscapes before returning to your hotel.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Shigar Fort
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana or Qayyam Hotel
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 4: Khaplu Valley

Travel to Khaplu Valley, enjoying scenic stops along the way. Visit Sailing Village and a local fish farm. Check in at your hotel, explore Khaplu Palace, and soak in the local culture.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Khaplu Palace
  • Luxury: Destination Hotel Khaplu
  • Standard: North Homes Khaplu

Day 5: Manthoka and Khamosh Waterfalls

Depart for the stunning Manthoka Waterfall, enjoying the scenic ride and multiple stops. Explore the waterfall’s beauty and spend leisure time before returning to Skardu.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Shigar Fort
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana or Qayyam Hotel
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 6: Bashu Valley

Embark on an adventurous off-road drive to the picturesque Bashu Valley. Explore the area’s serene beauty and enjoy free time before returning to Skardu.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Byarsa Hotel Skardu
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana or Qayyam Hotel
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 7: Return to Islamabad

Fly back to Islamabad, check into your hotel, and relax. Join our team for dinner and enjoy free time exploring the city.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 8: Islamabad City Tour

Explore Islamabad’s famous landmarks, including Faisal Mosque, Pakistan Monument, and Daman-e-Koh viewpoint. Enjoy leisurely free time to shop or unwind.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 9: Departure

Transfer to Islamabad International Airport for your return flight home, carrying cherished memories of Skardu’s incredible beauty.

Packing List

Packing Checklist for Northern Pakistan - Summit Experts

Traveling to the scenic mountains of Northern Pakistan during summer and autumn (June to mid-November) requires smart packing. The weather is cool and crisp, and the landscapes are stunning, making it an ideal time for a memorable journey. To ensure you have everything you need, here’s our recommended packing list.

Essential Packing Categories:

  1. Luggage & Bags
    • Main Bag (70-80L): A sturdy, spacious bag for all your essentials. Consider a duffel or rucksack with waterproof covers.
    • Carry-On/Daypack (30-40L): Ideal for carrying daily items and essentials during flights and local travel.
    • Padlocks: For added security during travel.
  2. Clothing
    • Upper Body:
      • Insulated Jacket: Lightweight but warm, perfect for layering.
      • Fleece or Soft Shell Jacket: To keep warm without feeling too bulky.
      • Long-Sleeve Shirts & T-Shirts: Preferably quick-drying fabrics.
    • Lower Body:
      • Trekking Trousers: Comfortable, quick-drying trousers suitable for hikes.
      • Thermal Underwear: For colder days and nights.
    • General Tips:
      • Layers are Key: Autumn weather can be unpredictable; layering helps you adjust to changes in temperature.
      • Modest Clothing: Covering shoulders and knees is recommended in urban areas and when visiting cultural sites.
  3. Footwear
    • Hiking Boots: Well-worn, waterproof boots with good ankle support.
    • Warm Socks: Opt for wool or moisture-wicking material.
    • Extra Laces: Just in case.
  4. Accessories
    • Sunglasses & Sunblock (SPF 50+): The sun can be strong, even in cooler weather.
    • Hat/Cap: For sun protection.
    • Warm Beanie: Essential for cooler mornings and evenings.
  5. Toiletries & Personal Care
    • Travel Towel & Wet Wipes: Compact and quick-drying options.
    • Basic Hygiene Kit: Include toothpaste, deodorant, lip balm, and moisturizers.
    • Hand Sanitizer & Masks: Always useful.
  6. Hydration & Snacks
    • Water Bottle (Insulated Recommended): Carry at least a 1L bottle for day trips.
    • Energy Snacks: Granola bars, dried fruits, and nuts for quick energy during hikes.
  7. Tech & Gadgets
    • Camera & Spare Batteries: Capture the beauty of autumn landscapes. Bring extra memory cards.
    • Power Bank: To keep devices charged during long excursions.
  8. Important Documents
    • Passport: With at least six months of validity and two blank pages.
    • Visa & Travel Insurance: Check requirements and ensure you have printouts of all travel documents.
    • Emergency Contacts: Keep a printed list of important contact numbers.

Tips for Autumn and summer Packing

  • Plan for Cool Nights: While days can be mild, temperatures drop quickly in the evenings. A warm jacket and thermal wear will be your best friends.
  • Pack Light but Smart: Choose versatile clothing that can be mixed and matched.
  • Respect Local Culture: While locals are friendly, it’s respectful to dress modestly, especially in towns and when visiting religious sites.

Why Travel with Summit Experts?

Our tours are designed with your comfort and safety in mind. We make sure you’re prepared for every aspect of your trip so that you can focus on enjoying the beauty of Northern Pakistan.

Overview

About Expedition

The Snow Lake Trek is an extraordinary journey to one of the most stunning yet least-visited places in the Karakoram. Snow Lake, a vast glacial basin at an altitude of 4,800m, is a hidden gem surrounded by towering ice walls and pristine landscapes. This trek follows the Biafo and Hispar Glaciers, offering adventurers the chance to walk on one of the longest glacial systems outside the polar regions.

Why This Trek?

  • True Wilderness Adventure: A remote and untouched glacial wonderland.
  • Breathtaking Ice Formations: Traverse one of the world’s longest glacier systems.
  • Wildlife & Unique Landscapes: Spot ibex, snow leopards, and other high-altitude wildlife.
  • A Hidden Gem: Experience an area few have set foot in, away from crowded trekking routes.

Itinerary

Day 01: Arrive in Islamabad

Altitude: 540 m

Details: Upon arrival at Islamabad International Airport, our team will greet you and assist with your transfer to the hotel, allowing you to rest after your journey. If you arrive between 9 AM and 12 PM, lunch will be provided, followed by some time to relax. In the evening, all trekkers will gather for a briefing session, covering the trek details, safety measures, and final preparations. If arriving late, the briefing will be conducted in Skardu.

Day 02: Fly to Skardu

Altitude: 2,498 m

Details: An early morning flight from Islamabad to Skardu offers stunning aerial views of the Himalayas and Karakoram, including Nanga Parbat (8,126m), the 9th highest mountain in the world. Upon arrival, you will have the rest of the day free to explore Skardu. In case of flight cancellation, an alternative road journey to Chilas will be arranged.

Day 03: Free Day in Skardu

Altitude: 2,498 m

Details: After breakfast, we embark on a scenic hike to Kharpocho Fort, offering panoramic views of Skardu town and the Indus River. You may also visit Sadpara Lake, a serene  high-altitude lake surrounded by mountains. Our team will complete the necessary government documentation for the trek, which may take up to two days.

Day 04: Drive to Askole Village

Altitude: 3,015 m

Details:  We begin our 6–8 hour jeep journey towards Askole, the last inhabited village before entering the wilderness. The route follows the Shigar Valley and the Braldu River, passing through dramatic gorges and traditional Balti settlements.

Day 05: Trek to Namla

Altitude: 3,571 m

Details: The trek officially begins as we leave Askole, following the K2 Base Camp trail before diverting west onto the Biafo Glacier. We ascend over a rocky shoulder to the left moraine and carefully navigate crevasses before setting up camp at Namla, a scenic grassy site behind a lateral moraine.

Day 06: Trek to Mango

Altitude: 3,715 m

Details: Today’s trek involves crossing a complex fracture zone of the glacier, moving along rugged moraine ridges. Expect challenging terrain with loose rocks, requiring focus and stability. We set up camp on the left bank of the Biafo Glacier, in a sheltered grassy area.

Day 07: Trek to Baintha

Altitude: 4,041 m

Details: Continuing along the glacier’s center, the trek becomes slightly easier compared to the previous days. The day ends at Baintha, a stunning camping spot surrounded by towering Karakoram peaks and grassy meadows.

Day 08: Acclimatization and Rest

Altitude: 4,041 m

Details: A well-earned rest day at Baintha allows trekkers to adjust to the high-altitude conditions. You may choose to hike up a ridge for panoramic views of Latok I & II and The Ogre, or relax in the campsite, keeping an eye out for wild ibex on the surrounding slopes.

Day 09: Trek to Morfogoro

Altitude: 4,298 m

Details: After breakfast, we embark on a steep ascent onto the glacier. The terrain flattens out, making for a relatively straightforward trek. As we progress, the dramatic Ogre Peak (7,285m) dominates the skyline, and we get our first glimpses of Snow Lake and Hispar La.

Day 10: Trek to Hispar La Base Camp

Altitude: 4,585 m

Details: We trek across the surreal Snow Lake, an enormous glacial basin that stretches as far as the eye can see. Navigation requires caution due to hidden crevasses. Named by Martin Conway in 1892, Snow Lake is considered one of the most beautiful glacier basins in the world.

Day 11: Cross Snow Lake to Hispar La

Altitude: 5,149 m

Details: Today, we ascend Hispar La, a high-altitude mountain pass linking Biafo and Hispar Glaciers. Though not extremely steep, the elevation makes the climb physically demanding. The views from the top are breathtaking, showcasing an endless sea of ice and peaks.

Day 12: Trek to Kani Basa

Altitude: 4,468 m

Details: We start early, descending from Hispar La into a maze of crevasses. The landscape transitions as we reach Kani Basa Glacier, where the confluence of two glaciers creates a dramatic setting for our camp.

Day 13: Trek to Jutmal

Altitude: 4,168 m

Details: A tough trekking day awaits as we cross moraine ridges, scramble up scree slopes, and wade through glacial streams. The reward is reaching Jutmal, a scenic campsite nestled between ice and rock.

Day 14: Trek to Bitanmal

Altitude: 3,765 m

Details: A steep descent takes us across another glacier before emerging into the valley below. We camp in Bitanmal, a large meadow used by local herders from Hispar Village.

Day 15: Trek to Falaling Chhish

Altitude: 3,605 m

Details: Our final glacier crossing over Kunyang Glacier leads us onto a well-defined trail, bringing us to the beautiful Falaling Chhish meadows.

Day 16: Trek to Hispar Village

Altitude: 2,297 m

Details: A bridge crossing marks the transition from glaciers to Hispar Village, where we are welcomed by lush orchards and terraced fields. Depending on road conditions, we either meet our jeeps for transfer or walk to the campsite.

Day 17: Drive to Karimabad

Altitude: 2,440 m

Details: We leave the wilderness behind, driving through Nagar Valley before joining the Karakoram Highway. Arriving in Karimabad, we check into our hotel and enjoy a well-earned rest.

Day 18: Contingency Day/Sightseeing

Details: Allocated for any potential trekking delays; enjoy a day of sightseeing in Hunza Valley.

Visit the historic Baltit and Altit forts, explore Karimabad, and admire the stunning landscapes.

Day 19: Fly to Islamabad

Altitude: 538 m

Details: Morning flight from Gilgit to Islamabad.If flights are canceled, an alternative drive to Naran or Besham will be arranged.

Day 20: Contingency Day for Flight Cancellations

Altitude: 538 m

Details: Allocate this day for potential flight delays, with an early morning departure to Islamabad if necessary. Free day in Islamabad for sightseeing if flights are successful.

Day 21: Departure

Meals Included: Breakfast

Details: Our staff will transfer you to the airport based on your flight schedule. Hotel checkout time is 12 PM.

Day 09: Trek to Morfogoro

Details: After breakfast, we embark on a steep ascent onto the glacier. The terrain flattens out, making for a relatively straightforward trek. As we progress, the dramatic Ogre Peak (7,285m) dominates the skyline, and we get our first glimpses of Snow Lake and Hispar La.

Day 10: Trek to Hispar La Base Camp

Altitude: 4,585 m

Details: We trek across the surreal Snow Lake, an enormous glacial basin that stretches as far as the eye can see. Navigation requires caution due to hidden crevasses. Named by Martin Conway in 1892, Snow Lake is considered one of the most beautiful glacier basins in the world.

Day 11: Cross Snow Lake to Hispar La

Altitude: 5,149 m

Details: Today, we ascend Hispar La, a high-altitude mountain pass linking Biafo and Hispar Glaciers. Though not extremely steep, the elevation makes the climb physically demanding. The views from the top are breathtaking, showcasing an endless sea of ice and peaks.

Day 12: Trek to Kani Basa

Altitude: 4,468 m

Details: We start early, descending from Hispar La into a maze of crevasses. The landscape transitions as we reach Kani Basa Glacier, where the confluence of two glaciers creates a dramatic setting for our camp.

Day 13: Trek to Jutmal

Altitude: 4,168 m

Details: A tough trekking day awaits as we cross moraine ridges, scramble up scree slopes, and wade through glacial streams. The reward is reaching Jutmal, a scenic campsite nestled between ice and rock.

Day 14: Trek to Bitanmal

Altitude: 3,765 m

Details: A steep descent takes us across another glacier before emerging into the valley below. We camp in Bitanmal, a large meadow used by local herders from Hispar Village.

Day 15: Trek to Falaling Chhish

Altitude: 3,605 m

Details: Our final glacier crossing over Kunyang Glacier leads us onto a well-defined trail, bringing us to the beautiful Falaling Chhish meadows.

Day 16: Trek to Hispar Village

Altitude: 2,297 m

Details: A bridge crossing marks the transition from glaciers to Hispar Village, where we are welcomed by lush orchards and terraced fields. Depending on road conditions, we either meet our jeeps for transfer or walk to the campsite.

Day 17: Drive to Karimabad

Altitude: 2,440 m

Details: We leave the wilderness behind, driving through Nagar Valley before joining the Karakoram Highway. Arriving in Karimabad, we check into our hotel and enjoy a well-earned rest.

Day 18: Contingency Day/Sightseeing

Details: Allocated for any potential trekking delays; enjoy a day of sightseeing in Hunza Valley.

Visit the historic Baltit and Altit forts, explore Karimabad, and admire the stunning landscapes.

Day 19: Fly to Islamabad

Altitude: 538 m

Details: Morning flight from Gilgit to Islamabad.If flights are canceled, an alternative drive to Naran or Besham will be arranged.

Day 20: Contingency Day for Flight Cancellations

Altitude: 538 m

Details: Allocate this day for potential flight delays, with an early morning departure to Islamabad if necessary. Free day in Islamabad for sightseeing if flights are successful.

Day 21: Departure

Meals Included: Breakfast

Details: Our staff will transfer you to the airport based on your flight schedule. Hotel checkout time is 12 PM.

Packing List

Embarking on the Snow Lake Trek requires careful preparation to ensure your safety, comfort, and success. We have categorized the required gear into three distinct lists to help you pack efficiently for this incredible adventure.

Essential Gear

  • These mandatory items are crucial for your trek and should be included in your packing list:

    • First Aid Kit: Diamox (for altitude sickness), Dioralyte (rehydration salts), antiseptic cream, blister treatment, throat lozenges, adhesive plasters, Imodium (for diarrhea), painkillers.
    • Backpack (Daypack): 32–42 liters.
    • Insulation & Clothing:
      • Fleece jacket with hood or a warm sweater.
      • Warm gloves or mittens.
      • Thermal gloves.
      • Baselayer thermal shirts (two long-sleeve, two short-sleeve).
      • Baselayer thermal leggings.
      • Trekking trousers.
      • Waterproof jacket.
      • Waterproof over-trousers.
      • Shirts/T-shirts.
      • Walking socks (2–3 pairs).
      • Spare laces.
      • Underwear (regular and thermal).
    • Footwear:
      • High-quality hiking boots.
      • Sports sandals or old shoes (for river crossings).
    • Headgear & Accessories:
      • Warm hat.
      • Sun hat.
      • Sunglasses.
      • Headtorch with spare batteries.
    • Camping & Sleeping Gear:
      • Sleeping bag (-16°C comfort rating).
      • Sleeping mat (Thermarest or equivalent).
    • Hydration & Hygiene:
      • Water bottles (1 liter × 2).
      • Antibacterial hand wash.
      • Small towel.
      • Wash bag and toiletries.
    • Additional Essentials:
      • Trekking poles (highly recommended).
      • Down jacket (warm).
      • Mountaineering equipment (see List 2 below).

Mountaineering Equipment

  • For theSnow Lake Trek, additional technical gear is required:

    • Crampons.
    • Mountaineering boots (must be compatible with crampons, minimum Grade B2).
    • Ice axe.
    • Climbing harness.
    • Screwgate carabiners (x2).
    • Climbing helmet.
    • Prusik loops (x2) (4 meters of 6mm cord can be used to make two loops).
    • 120 cm sling.

Optional Items

While not mandatory, these items may add comfort and convenience to your trekking experience:

  • Buff or scarf.
  • Small padlock (for securing your bag).
  • Camera.
  • Insect repellent.
  • Multi-tool or pen knife (must be packed in checked luggage).
  • Basic repair kit (thread, needle, duct tape, etc.).
  • Sleeping bag liner.
  • Travel clothes for pre- and post-trek.
  • Bottle for personal hygiene (pee bottle).

FAQs

01

What are the best months for trekking in Pakistan?

+

 The best trekking season is from June to September, when temperatures are stable, and most passes are snow-free. For treks involving Gondogoro La Pass, July and August offer and for Snow Lake August is the safest conditions.

02

How physically demanding are these treks?

+

Each trek varies in difficulty:

  • K2 Base Camp Trek – Strenuous but non-technical, requiring good fitness.
  • Snow Lake Trek – Challenging due to glacier travel and isolation.
  • K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La Circuit Trek – Demanding, with technical sections requiring crampons.
03

Do I need prior trekking experience?

+

Experience is not mandatory but recommended. You should be comfortable walking 6-8 hours per day on rocky and glacial terrain. Proper physical preparation is essential.

04

What permits do I need?

+
  • K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La Trek require a special Mountaineering & Trekking Visa (not a regular tourist visa).
  • Snow Lake Trek requires a regular visa as this is not located in a restricted zone, which we arrange for you.
05

What happens in case of an emergency?

+
  • Our guides carry satellite phones for emergencies.
  • If altitude sickness occurs, you will be escorted to a lower altitude.
  • In severe cases, a helicopter rescue can be arranged (insurance required).
06

What fitness level and skills are required for K2 Treks?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: Suitable for fit individuals with previous hiking experience. Trekkers walk 6-8 miles per day for 5-6 hours on rough terrain.

Gondogoro La Pass: Requires use of crampons and ropes due to snow, ice, and steeper climbs.

07

How far will we walk each day?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: Expect to walk 8 to 14 km per day, taking 6-8 hours.
  • Gondogoro La Pass: The crossing day can take 8-12 hours, depending on snow conditions.
08

What’s the most challenging section of the trek?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: The trek from Concordia to K2 Base Camp is challenging due to altitude and glacier terrain.
  • Gondogoro La Pass: The most difficult part is the steep ascent and descent over icy slopes.
09

What makes the Snow Lake Trek unique?

+

 This is one of the most remote and scenic glacier treks in the world. The landscape features massive ice fields, crevasses, and towering peaks.

10

How technical is this trek?

+

 Snow Lake requires glacier travel skills but is non-technical. Crampons are highly recommended.

11

What is the duration of the trek?

+

The expedition takes 16-20 days, depending on weather and glacier conditions.

12

Are guides and porters included?

+
  • Yes, our experienced guides and porters ensure safety and logistics throughout the trek.

Overview

About Expedition

The Spantik Peak Expedition is an incredible 31-day adventure into the Shigar Valley, leading to the breathtaking Golden Peak (7,027m). This expedition is an ideal choice for mountaineers looking to scale a 7,000m+ peak with a manageable technical challenge. The journey begins in Skardu, taking adventurers through Arandu Village, Chogolungma Glacier, and to Spantik Base Camp, where climbers prepare for the summit push. This expedition offers stunning glacier crossings, high-altitude camping, and unparalleled views of the Karakoram Range.

Why This Expedition?

  • Golden Peak Challenge: Conquer a 7,027m summit known for its striking golden glow at sunrise and sunset.
  • Perfect for Aspiring 7,000m Climbers: A great training peak for those aiming for 8,000m expeditions.
  • Dramatic Glacial Terrain: Trek across the Chogolungma and Bolocho Glaciers, navigating their rugged beauty.
  • Breathtaking Views: Witness majestic panoramas of K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum, and other Karakoram giants.
  • A True Alpine Experience: Experience the thrill of technical ice and snow climbing, with expert guidance from Summit Experts.

Itinerary

Day 01: Arrive at Islamabad International Airport

Altitude: 540 m

Details: Upon arrival at Islamabad International Airport, our team will greet you and assist with your transfer to the hotel. You will have time to rest and recover from your journey. In the evening, a detailed expedition briefing will be conducted, covering all essential aspects of the trip. If you arrive early, you will have the opportunity to explore the city.

Day 02: Fly to Skardu, Karakoram

Altitude: 2,498 m

Details:Weather permitting, we take a spectacular mountain flight from Islamabad to Skardu, offering breathtaking views of Nanga Parbat (8,126m). In case of flight cancellations due to weather, we begin an alternative two-day drive to Skardu, stopping overnight in Chilas.

Day 03: Free Day in Skardu

Altitude: 2,498 m

Details: If arriving by flight, this day will be spent finalizing expedition permits, organizing gear, and exploring Skardu Bazaar. If traveling by road, we complete the final leg of the journey, arriving in Skardu in the afternoon.

Day 04: Drive to Arandu Village

Altitude: 2,720 m

Details: A 6–7 hour jeep ride takes us along the Shigar River to Arandu Village, the last settlement before heading into the mountains. The route offers incredible views of desert valleys, rugged peaks, and high-altitude villages.

Day 05: Trek to Chogo Brangsa Camp

Altitude: 3,400 m

Details: Leaving Arandu, we begin our trek across moraines, glacial streams, and rocky paths. The terrain is rugged, but the views of Spantik and surrounding peaks make the journey rewarding. After a 5–6 hour trek, we arrive at Chogo Brangsa for our first night under the stars.

Day 06: Trek to Bolocho Camp

Altitude: 3,820 m

Details: The trek today involves traversing the Bolocho Glacier, requiring careful navigation over crevasses and shifting ice formations. The landscape is otherworldly, with towering ice walls and deep glacial valleys. Camp is set up at Bolocho, offering spectacular sunset views over the surrounding peaks.

Day 07: Trek to Spantik Base Camp

Altitude: 4,360 m

Details: A steep ascent takes us onto the Chogolungma Glacier, where we make our final push toward Spantik Base Camp. The journey takes 6–7 hours, leading to a dramatic setting with panoramic views of Spantik’s Golden Pillar. We establish our base camp here, preparing for the upcoming ascent.

Day 08: Acclimatization at Spantik Base Camp

Altitude: 4,360 m

Details: The following days are dedicated to acclimatization, technical climbing training, and summit attempts. We establish high camps at 5,100m, 5,800m, and 6,300m, gradually making our way toward the final summit push. Depending on weather conditions and climbers’ readiness, we attempt to reach the summit of Spantik, experiencing an unparalleled 360° panorama of the Karakoram Range

Days 09-25: Climbing Days

Details: Enjoy 16 days dedicated to climbing the peak, with ample opportunities for acclimatization and preparation.

Day 26: Departure from Base Camp

Details:  The team, along with Summit Experts Tours staff, will leave base camp and begin the trek back. The descent via the Chogolungma Glacier will take approximately 8-9 hours.

Day 27: Trek to Arandu Village

Altitude: 2,720 m

Details: The final leg of our trek brings us back to Arandu Village, where we reconnect with civilization. Here, we celebrate the successful completion of the climb with the local Balti community.

Day 28: Drive to Skardu

Altitude: 2,250 m

Details: A 6–7 hour jeep ride takes us back to Skardu, where we enjoy well-earned rest, hot showers, and a final team dinner to commemorate the adventure.

Day 29: Fly to Islamabad

Altitude: 538 m

Details: We’ll take a morning flight from Skardu to Islamabad. Enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the hotel. Note that Domestic flights may occasionally be canceled due to weather. In such cases, an overnight stay in Chilas will be arranged (8-10 hours by vehicle).

Day 30: Contingency Day for Flight Cancellations

Details: This day serves as a buffer for potential flight delays. If needed, guests will depart early from Chilas to Islamabad (up to 10 hours of travel). If the flight is successful, this day can be used for sightseeing in Islamabad.

Day 31: Departure

Meals Included: Breakfast

Details: Our staff will transfer all guests to the airport based on their respective departure timings. Checkout time at partner hotels is 12 PM.

Packing List

Bags & Packs

  1. Kit bag: One or two large duffel bags of 120L or more (some climbers manage with one, others need two) to transport your kit out to Pakistan and then up to Spantik basecamp. Suitcases and wheeled bags are NOT suitable.
  2. Expedition rucksack: Approximately 70-80L to take your kit from basecamp to higher camps, carrying up to 15kg. Make sure it has a waterproof cover.
  3. Daysack: 30-40L for flights and road transfers. You can use your expedition rucksack instead if you do not want to take this pack. Some do, some don’t, it’s a personal choice.
  4. Dry stuffsacks: Rolltop bags that keep fresh clothing and other important items lime your passports and electronics dry in the event of a total downpour that could seep into your kitbag. Good for quarantining old socks! Please note that Pakistan has now banned plastic bags. In any case, we would always advise buying reusable and sustainable nylon rolltop bags for keeping your kit dry.
  5. Small kit bag or light bag: This is for any kit you intend to leave at the hotel and could even simply be a heavy duty plastic bag if necessary, as you will be taking it home with you. Do note that Pakistan have banned the sale of single-use plastic bags so if you have something reusable this would be preferable.
  6. Padlocks x 2: For use on your kit bag during travel and on the expedition, plus any bag you may leave at the hotel.

Sleeping Gear

  1. 5 Season sleeping bag: A 5-season bag with a comfort rating to -25°C is essential. Down is lighter, though more expensive than synthetic. Remember that ratings may vary between manufacturers.
  2. Sleeping mat: We would recommend a full length self-inflating mat, eg. Thermarest, rather than a 3/4 length mat.
  3. Sleeping bag liner: A liner will help keep your sleeping bag clean and provide extra warmth. Silk is best for keeping you a little warmer.

Headwear

  1. Warm headgear x 2: This can be a warm hat, beanie or balaclava – anything to reduce the heat loss from your head.
  2. Wide brimmed hat: Keeps the sun off exposed areas such as your ears, or the nape of your neck.
  3. Sunglasses: A Category-4 wrap around style is highly recommended. These sunglasses allow for the highest available protection against harmful UV light found at altitude and from glare from snow and sand surfaces. It’s worth spending money on good UV filters. Julbo is our preferred supplier.
  4. Ski goggles: We’d recommend Category-3 for days when it may be snowing and very windy. Generally very useful on summit day.
  5. Sunblock: We’d advise factor 50 for trekking – but otherwise buy the highest SPF you can find, as UV intensifies with altitude.
  6. Buff/Scarf: Essential for protection from the sun and dust.
  7. Lip salve: Sun cream generally does not work on your lips and they are very susceptible to burning without proper protection, so it’s important to also have high SPF lipsalve.

Upper Body

  1. Base layer x 3: This is the layer closest to the skin and its principle function is to draw or wick moisture and sweat away from the skin. You can also get thermal base layers for use at higher altitudes that provide an additional insulating layer while still drawing away sweat during times of high exertion.
  2. Mid layer x 2: These are typically lightweight microfleeces or similar technology that provide varying degrees of warmth and insulation without being overly bulky or heavy to pack.
  3. Soft Shell (optional): Optional – These should be windproof (not all are) and insulative. They are mostly made of soft polyester and sometimes resemble a neoprene finish which makes them very mobile and comfortable to wear. Be aware that while they do offer a degree of weather repellence, they are usually not waterproof.
  4. Light insulated jacket: A lighter jacket such as a Primaloft or lightweight down, which can be worn at lower to mid altitudes, is a great addition to your kit and offers greater flexibility with layering.
  5. Gilet (optional): Optional – A great low-volume additional layer to keep your core warm, whether down, primaloft or fleece.
  6. Waterproof top: A good Goretex hardshell jacket, with sealed seams, provides effective defence against wind and rain as your outermost layer. This should be big enough to fit over your other layers.
  7. Down jacket: These provide the best insulation and are worth every penny. They will keep you warm down to around -25C with a couple of layers underneath, the higher the ‘loft’, the better. Our guides usually wear a lighter down or Primaloft jacket underneath their down jackets for greater layering on summit day.
  8. Warm gloves: Consider a light polartec pair or, better still, liner gloves for lower altitudes and evenings as well as a thicker pair like ski gloves for higher altitudes that can be worn in combination with liners.
  9. High altitude down mitts: Worn over liners for summit days on all 6,000m plus expeditions. Mitts provide more warmth than finger gloves. For extreme cold, down or Primaloft fill is recommended.
  10. Waterproof mitts: A great addition for an added windproof or waterproof layer, to fit either over your down mitts high up or your gloves lower down, especially as down ceases to work when it gets wet and takes a long time to dry. Synthetic fill dries much more quickly.

Lower Body

  1. Trekking trousers x 2: These tend to be polyester so they dry quickly after a shower and weigh little in your pack. Consider perhaps a pair with detachable lower legs as an alternative to shorts.
  2. Midweight trousers: These tend to be polyester so they dry quickly after a shower and weigh little in your pack. Consider perhaps a pair with detachable lower legs, as an alternative to shorts.
  3. Waterproof overtrousers: Along with the waterproof jacket, these are an essential piece of kit to keep you dry. They should also be Goretex and hardshell.
  4. Long Johns x 2: An essential thermal insulation layer for your legs.
  5. Underwear: Merino or wicking material is best, we’d advise against cotton. How many pairs you take is entirely up to you!

Feet

  1. High altitude boots: Essential on all our high altitude expeditions, as they are the only way to avoid frostbite. Commonly known as ‘plastics’, these boots are double or triple layered to offer the best insulation and the warmest feet up high. Either La Sportiva G2 SMs, Scarpa Phantom 8000s, La Sportiva Spantiks or more specialised 8,000m boots such as Olympus Mons are suitable. Make sure that your boots fit with 2 pairs of socks for added warmth, with room to wiggle your toes. Avoid trying to break in the boots by training in them, they will break you! Wear them around the house instead, to get used to the weight and feel.
  2. Walking boots: Well-worn in 4-season waterproof boots, with mid to high ankle support.
  3. Trekking socks x 4: Lighter weight merino wool is a good option. Going for a single layer or wearing two pairs is a personal choice.
  4. High altitude socks x 3: These are especially thick to provide maximum insulation. Bring three pairs (keep one pair clean for summit day!) and wear with a thinner inner.
  5. High altitude inner socks: Lightweight inner socks. Merino wool is advisable.
  6. Spare laces: Just in case.
  7. Gaiters: Protect the tops of your footwear from harsh conditions and provide some added insulation.
  8.  

Technical Equipment

  1. High altitude boots: Essential on all our high altitude expeditions, as they are the only way to avoid frostbite. Commonly known as ‘plastics’, these boots are double or triple layered to offer the best insulation and the warmest feet up high. Either La Sportiva G2 SMs, Scarpa Phantom 8000s, La Sportiva Spantiks or more specialised 8,000m boots such as Olympus Mons are suitable. Make sure that your boots fit with 2 pairs of socks for added warmth, with room to wiggle your toes. Avoid trying to break in the boots by training in them, they will break you! Wear them around the house instead, to get used to the weight and feel.
  2. Walking boots: Well-worn in 4-season waterproof boots, with mid to high ankle support.
  3. Trekking socks x 4: Lighter weight merino wool is a good option. Going for a single layer or wearing two pairs is a personal choice.
  4. High altitude socks x 3: These are especially thick to provide maximum insulation. Bring three pairs (keep one pair clean for summit day!) and wear with a thinner inner.
  5. High altitude inner socks: Lightweight inner socks. Merino wool is advisable.
  6. Spare laces: Just in case.
  7. Gaiters: Protect the tops of your footwear from harsh conditions and provide some added insulation.

Hydration

  1. Water bottle and insulated bottle cover: 3L equivalent – a good combination is a Platypus/Camelbak along with 2 x 1L Nalgene bottles. Use the Platypus before the water starts to freeze at higher camps!
  2. Water purification: Although generally all water is boiled, some prefer to double up and add purification tabs as well. They’re always good to have in your bag. If you’re using tablets, it’s worth taking neutraliser or using Silver Chloride as it has little taste.
  3. Insulated mug: A great addition for hot drinks at the higher camps.
  4. Small thermal flask: Always nice on summit night when it’s cold.
  5. Pee bottle (+ optional Shewee for the girls!): A good idea if you are storm bound at higher camps. A 1L Nalgene bottle is a good option but do make sure you label it appropriately!

Toiletries

  1. Travel towel: Travel towels from the likes of LifeSystems are perfect.
  2. Wet wipes: Preferably biodegradable, these are great for washing when modern shower facilities become a thing of the past.
  3. Alcohol gel: An absolute must-have for good camp hygiene.
  4. Toilet paper: Provided on the mountain, but a spare in your daysack may be useful if you need to hide behind a rock between camps.
  5. Nappy sacks or dog poo bags: Only needed to bag your toilet paper if you are caught short in between camps, or for keeping your rubbish tidy in your tent.
  6. Insect repellent: For early stages and once back down.
  7. Wash kit: Keep it simple on the mountain. Essentials are toothbrush, toothpaste and deodorant. Moisturiser is advisable, everything else is a luxury!

Medications

  1. Personal first aid kit: Though your guide will have a basic first aid kit, we recommend you come prepared with useful meds for yourself such as painkillers (Ibuprofen if you can take it and Paracetamol), plus blister plasters, plasters, antiseptic, rehydration sachets and any muscle rubs you wish to use.
  2. Personal medication: Keep this in your daysack.

Miscellaneous

  1. Head torch: We recommend Petzl head torches. Bring spare batteries.
  2. Camera: Bring plenty of spare memory cards, and spare batteries – cold temperatures deplete battery power rapidly and recharging might not be possible above basecamp. The trek can be dusty so some sort of protective camera bag is advisable.
  3. Penknife (optional)
  4. Sewing kit (optional)
  5. Hand warmers: For summit day
  6. Snacks: You will be fed very well and given plenty of snacks each day. However, we do advise bringing a small selection as a bit of comfort. For summit night it’s always good to have a few extra chunky bars or goodies that you particularly like for that extra boost. Energy gels and protein bars are not suitable for this expedition.

Other Checklist/Documentation

  1. Passport: Do not forget this! Your passport should have at least 6 months validity: ie. your passport expiry date needs to be at least six months after the final day of travel. Make sure you also have at least two blank pages.
  2. Copies of passport: Just in case.
  3. Passport photos x 4: We will need these to obtain your climbing and trekking permits.
  4. Visa: You will need to apply for a mountaineering and trekking visa for Pakistan at least 6 weeks before travel – it’s easiest to apply online: https://visa.nadra.gov.pk/ A 90-day, single entry visa for a UK trekker is currently US $60, but do check for the updated info.
  5. Dental check up: We recommend you have a dental check-up before your trip. New fillings can be an issue at altitude if there is an air pocket left in the gap.
  6. Money: We recommend you take around US $250 – $400 with you on to the mountain, in small denominations, to tip the Balti team. Plus, about $200 for any extras along the way, satellite phone calls etc. You may wish to bring extra for additional spending such as beers or souvenirs and to cover meals not included in the expedition price.
  7. Travel insurance: Bring a copy of your own travel insurance details along with relevant contact numbers. We recommend looking into deals offered by Global Rescue, True Traveller, the BMC, Austrian Alpine Club or similar insurers. Team members should take out private insurance that covers against cancellation due to medical or personal reasons and it is important that the insurance contains coverage for medical evacuations by helicopter or other means. Many other insurance providers are available and we do recommend that you shop around to get the best cover for you on the expedition you are undertaking. It is your responsibility to ensure that you have the appropriate insurance for your intended trip, which must include medical evacuation and coverage up to the maximum altitude of this expedition. Please contact the office if you have any queries about insurance for this trip.

Packing List

Bags & Packs

  1. Kit bag: One or two large duffel bags of 120L or more (some climbers manage with one, others need two) to transport your kit out to Pakistan and then up to Spantik basecamp. Suitcases and wheeled bags are NOT suitable.
  2. Expedition rucksack: Approximately 70-80L to take your kit from basecamp to higher camps, carrying up to 15kg. Make sure it has a waterproof cover.
  3. Daysack: 30-40L for flights and road transfers. You can use your expedition rucksack instead if you do not want to take this pack. Some do, some don’t, it’s a personal choice.
  4. Dry stuffsacks: Rolltop bags that keep fresh clothing and other important items lime your passports and electronics dry in the event of a total downpour that could seep into your kitbag. Good for quarantining old socks! Please note that Pakistan has now banned plastic bags. In any case, we would always advise buying reusable and sustainable nylon rolltop bags for keeping your kit dry.
  5. Small kit bag or light bag: This is for any kit you intend to leave at the hotel and could even simply be a heavy duty plastic bag if necessary, as you will be taking it home with you. Do note that Pakistan have banned the sale of single-use plastic bags so if you have something reusable this would be preferable.
  6. Padlocks x 2: For use on your kit bag during travel and on the expedition, plus any bag you may leave at the hotel.

Sleeping Gear

  1. 5 Season sleeping bag: A 5-season bag with a comfort rating to -25°C is essential. Down is lighter, though more expensive than synthetic. Remember that ratings may vary between manufacturers.
  2. Sleeping mat: We would recommend a full length self-inflating mat, eg. Thermarest, rather than a 3/4 length mat.
  3. Sleeping bag liner: A liner will help keep your sleeping bag clean and provide extra warmth. Silk is best for keeping you a little warmer.

Headwear

  1. Warm headgear x 2: This can be a warm hat, beanie or balaclava – anything to reduce the heat loss from your head.
  2. Wide brimmed hat: Keeps the sun off exposed areas such as your ears, or the nape of your neck.
  3. Sunglasses: A Category-4 wrap around style is highly recommended. These sunglasses allow for the highest available protection against harmful UV light found at altitude and from glare from snow and sand surfaces. It’s worth spending money on good UV filters. Julbo is our preferred supplier.
  4. Ski goggles: We’d recommend Category-3 for days when it may be snowing and very windy. Generally very useful on summit day.
  5. Sunblock: We’d advise factor 50 for trekking – but otherwise buy the highest SPF you can find, as UV intensifies with altitude.
  6. Buff/Scarf: Essential for protection from the sun and dust.
  7. Lip salve: Sun cream generally does not work on your lips and they are very susceptible to burning without proper protection, so it’s important to also have high SPF lipsalve.

Upper Body

  1. Base layer x 3: This is the layer closest to the skin and its principle function is to draw or wick moisture and sweat away from the skin. You can also get thermal base layers for use at higher altitudes that provide an additional insulating layer while still drawing away sweat during times of high exertion.
  2. Mid layer x 2: These are typically lightweight microfleeces or similar technology that provide varying degrees of warmth and insulation without being overly bulky or heavy to pack.
  3. Soft Shell (optional): Optional – These should be windproof (not all are) and insulative. They are mostly made of soft polyester and sometimes resemble a neoprene finish which makes them very mobile and comfortable to wear. Be aware that while they do offer a degree of weather repellence, they are usually not waterproof.
  4. Light insulated jacket: A lighter jacket such as a Primaloft or lightweight down, which can be worn at lower to mid altitudes, is a great addition to your kit and offers greater flexibility with layering.
  5. Gilet (optional): Optional – A great low-volume additional layer to keep your core warm, whether down, primaloft or fleece.
  6. Waterproof top: A good Goretex hardshell jacket, with sealed seams, provides effective defence against wind and rain as your outermost layer. This should be big enough to fit over your other layers.
  7. Down jacket: These provide the best insulation and are worth every penny. They will keep you warm down to around -25C with a couple of layers underneath, the higher the ‘loft’, the better. Our guides usually wear a lighter down or Primaloft jacket underneath their down jackets for greater layering on summit day.
  8. Warm gloves: Consider a light polartec pair or, better still, liner gloves for lower altitudes and evenings as well as a thicker pair like ski gloves for higher altitudes that can be worn in combination with liners.
  9. High altitude down mitts: Worn over liners for summit days on all 6,000m plus expeditions. Mitts provide more warmth than finger gloves. For extreme cold, down or Primaloft fill is recommended.
  10. Waterproof mitts: A great addition for an added windproof or waterproof layer, to fit either over your down mitts high up or your gloves lower down, especially as down ceases to work when it gets wet and takes a long time to dry. Synthetic fill dries much more quickly.

Lower Body

  1. Trekking trousers x 2: These tend to be polyester so they dry quickly after a shower and weigh little in your pack. Consider perhaps a pair with detachable lower legs as an alternative to shorts.
  2. Midweight trousers: These tend to be polyester so they dry quickly after a shower and weigh little in your pack. Consider perhaps a pair with detachable lower legs, as an alternative to shorts.
  3. Waterproof overtrousers: Along with the waterproof jacket, these are an essential piece of kit to keep you dry. They should also be Goretex and hardshell.
  4. Long Johns x 2: An essential thermal insulation layer for your legs.
  5. Underwear: Merino or wicking material is best, we’d advise against cotton. How many pairs you take is entirely up to you!

Feet

Make sure that your boots fit with 2 pairs of socks for added warmth, with room to wiggle your toes. Avoid trying to break in the boots by training in them, they will break you! Wear them around the house instead, to get used to the weight and feel.
  2. Walking boots: Well-worn in 4-season waterproof boots, with mid to high ankle support.
  3. Trekking socks x 4: Lighter weight merino wool is a good option. Going for a single layer or wearing two pairs is a personal choice.
  4. High altitude socks x 3: These are especially thick to provide maximum insulation. Bring three pairs (keep one pair clean for summit day!) and wear with a thinner inner.
  5. High altitude inner socks: Lightweight inner socks. Merino wool is advisable.
  6. Spare laces: Just in case.
  7. Gaiters: Protect the tops of your footwear from harsh conditions and provide some added insulation.

FAQs

01

What is included in the Base Camp Service and what is not?

+

The Base Camp Service for Spantik Expedition includes essential logistical support up to base camp, but does not cover high-altitude climbing assistance or personal expedition gear.

 Included in Base Camp Service:

  • All meals during the trek to base camp & at base camp (B, L, D)
  • Lodging at base camp
  • Full base camp setup (dining tent, mess tent, and bathroom)
  • All domestic transport & flights
  • 50kg (110 lbs) personal baggage allowance
  • Permit & royalty fees
  • Group emergency equipment & satellite phone (fixed call charge applies)
  • Staff insurance (guides, cooks, kitchen staff, porters, etc.)
  • Experienced Pakistani cook & kitchen staff
  • Porters for all expedition supplies
  • Solar power at base camp
  • Backup electricity generator for high-voltage devices

 Not Included in Base Camp Service:

  • High-altitude climbing leader
  • Rope fixers/porters for above base camp
  • Lodging above base camp
  • Group climbing gear/equipment (tents, ropes, cooking stoves, etc.)
  • Meals above base camp (high-altitude food/snacks)
  • High-altitude porters for group equipment
  • Personal high-altitude porter (HAP) from Pakistan
  • Supplemental oxygen cylinders & oxygen set
  • International airfare & personal climbing equipment
  • Mountain rescue & evacuation insurance (mandatory)
  • Pakistan visa fee & tips for staff
  • Extra hotel nights before/after the expedition
  • Trip cancellation insurance & personal communication costs
02

What is included in the Full Board Service and what is not?

+

The Full Board Service for Spantik Expedition provides comprehensive logistical and climbing support, ensuring a fully guided experience from base camp to the summit.

 Included in Full Board Service:

  • Everything included in the Base Camp Service
  • High-altitude climbing leader from Pakistan
  • Rope fixers/porters for group equipment above base camp
  • Lodging above base camp
  • Group climbing gear (tents, ropes, ice screws, gas, cooking stoves, etc.)
  • Meals above base camp (high-altitude food/snacks)
  • High-altitude porters for group equipment

Not Included in Full Board Service:

  • Personal high-altitude porter (HAP) from Pakistan ($1,400 extra cost)
  • Supplemental oxygen (1 cylinder recommended at $990 new, $650 used)
  • Oxygen set for climbers (includes regulator, mask, and hoses - $980)
  • Summit bonus for personal HAP ($200 extra cost)
  • International airfare & personal climbing equipment
  • Mountain rescue & evacuation insurance (mandatory)
  • Pakistan visa fee & tips for staff ($390 total)
  • Extra hotel nights before/after the expedition
  • Trip cancellation insurance & any additional expenses due to early summit or evacuation
  • Charges due to force majeure delays (e.g., weather-related cancellations)
  • Personal communication (phone, fax, email) between Pakistan & home country
03

What are the weather conditions like for each climb?

+

 Weather conditions vary depending on the mountain and season. Typically, the best climbing window is between June and September, when conditions are more stable. However, strong winds, snowfall, and sub-zero temperatures are still common at high altitudes.

04

How do I train for high-altitude climbing?

+
  • Climbers should prepare with a combination of cardio endurance, strength training, and altitude acclimatization. We recommend long hikes with a weighted pack, stair training, and high-altitude simulations if possible.
05

What kind of food will be provided at base camp and high camps?

+
  • We provide a mix of Pakistani, Western, and high-energy expedition meals. Base camp meals include fresh vegetables, meats, pasta, rice, and soups, while high camps rely on freeze-dried and lightweight meals for easy preparation.
06

How much weight will I need to carry during the climb?

+
    • For Khosar Gang and Spantik, you will carry a light daypack (5-8kg) while porters transport heavier loads.
    For Broad Peak, climbers carry their own gear above base camp, typically 12-15kg including climbing equipment.
07

Can I hire a personal climbing guide or high-altitude porter?

+
  •  Yes, personal guides and porters are available at an additional cost. We highly recommend hiring a high-altitude porter for Broad Peak due to the extreme difficulty of carrying heavy loads above 7,000m.
08

What type of insurance do I need?

+
  • Climbers must have comprehensive insurance covering high-altitude mountaineering, emergency rescue, and medical evacuation. A helicopter evacuation in the Karakoram can cost between $20,000 and $32,000 USD, so proper coverage is essential.
09

What happens if the weather prevents a summit attempt?

+

 If the weather prevents a summit bid, we will wait for a safer window or descend and return if necessary. Expedition dates include buffer days for flexibility, but we always prioritize safety over reaching the summit.

10

How technical is Spantik Peak?

+

 Spantik is considered a moderate-level climb. While it does not require advanced technical skills, climbers should be comfortable with using ropes, ice axes, and crampons on steep glacier terrain.

11

What prior experience do I need?

+
  • At least one prior climb above 5,000m or extensive high-altitude trekking experience.

Familiarity with fixed ropes, belaying, and basic self-arrest techniques.

12

What is the duration of the Spantik expedition?

+

  • The standard Spantik expedition takes 30 days, allowing for proper acclimatization and multiple summit attempts if necessary.

13

Is oxygen required for this climb?

+

 No, oxygen is not required, but we carry emergency oxygen for safety.

14

Do I need a climbing permit for Spantik?

+

 Yes, a mountaineering permit is required, which we will arrange on your behalf. The new permit price per person is USD 2,000.

15

What is the success rate for summiting Spantik?

+

 Spantik has a high success rate (approximately 70%), making it a great choice for climbers looking to gain experience before attempting higher peaks.
